   311	/-- The conditional divisor datum cut by a base-changed presentation section.
   312	
   313	The explicit `hsec` hypothesis is the non-vacuous fibrewise nonvanishing input.  It is
   314	converted componentwise to the injectivity required by the fibrewise-regular section
   315	construction; the integral fibre instance is installed from the standing geometrically
   316	irreducible curve hypotheses.
   317	-/
   318	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   319	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   320	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   321	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   322	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   323	    (hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   324	      (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   325	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0) :
   326	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
   327	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   328	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   329	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   330	  D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s
   331	    (fun j q => by
   332	      letI : IsIntegral (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   333	        instIsIntegralBaseChange C q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   334	      exact D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero s q (hsec q) j)
   335	
   336	/-- The conditional section construction preserves the base-changed datum's Picard class. -/
   337	theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange_picClass
   338	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   339	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   340	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   341	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   342	    (hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   343	      (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   344	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0) :
   345	    (P.sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange B y hsec).picClass =
   346	      (P.datum.baseChange B).cechPicClass := by
   347	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   348	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   349	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   350	  unfold sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   351	  exact D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass s
   352	    (fun j q => by
   353	      letI : IsIntegral (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   354	        instIsIntegralBaseChange C q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   355	      exact D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero s q (hsec q) j)

   357	/-- The presentation identifies datum `H^0` with native global sections of its line bundle. -/
   358	noncomputable def moduleSectionsEquiv (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
   359	    Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ≃ₗ[P.cover.Carrier] Γ(P.module, ⊤) :=
   360	  (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv P.module_iso.symm 0).trans
   361	    (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   362	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   363	      isTerminalTop
   364	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   365	        (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module))
   366	
   367	/-- The native section is exactly the datum section transported through `module_iso`. -/
   368	theorem module_iso_inv_datumSection (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   369	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   370	    (P.module_iso.inv.hom.app (op (⊤ : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens))).hom
   371	      (P.datumSection y) = P.moduleSectionsEquiv y := by
   372	  exact Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀_naturality
   373	    (hT := isTerminalTop) (f := P.module_iso.inv) y

   375	/-- A datum `H^0` class, read as a global section of the native pushforward. -/
   376	noncomputable def pushforwardSectionOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   377	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   378	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   379	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module, ⊤) := by
   380	  change Γ(P.module,
   381	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   382	      (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))
   383	  simpa using P.moduleSectionsEquiv y

   385	/-- The canonical unit-lift of a datum `H^0` class to the source of evaluation. -/
   386	noncomputable def evaluationLiftOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   387	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   388	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
   389	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
   390	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   391	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module),
   392	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   393	        (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens)) :=
   394	  ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   395	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).unit.app
   396	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   397	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)).app
   398	          (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens) (P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y)
   399	
   400	/-- Evaluation of the canonical unit-lift returns the original native global section.
   401	
   402	This is the right triangle identity of pullback-pushforward.  It is the counit compatibility
   403	needed before the section can be used to define a divisor; no zero-locus claim is made here. -/
   404	theorem evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   405	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   406	    (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
   407	      ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   408	        (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
   409	      (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y) = P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y := by
   410	  have h := congrArg
   411	    (fun (f : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   412	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module ⟶
   413	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   414	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) =>
   415	      (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app f (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens)).hom
   416	        (P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y))
   417	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   418	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).right_triangle_components
   419	        P.module)
   420	  exact h

   422	/-! ## Local-away generators for the canonical evaluation -/
   423	
   424	/-- Nonvanishing on every residue-field fibre of `D(f)` survives passage from the
   425	corresponding prime of the original ring to the residue field of a prime of `A_f`.
   426	
   427	The residue-field comparison is an isomorphism because localization induces bijective
   428	residue-field maps.  Keeping this as a private module lemma prevents the rank-one
   429	construction from depending on a false definitional transitivity of datum base change. -/
   430	private theorem fibre_tmul_ne_zero_of_away
   431	    {A Q : Type u} [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q]
   432	    (f : A) (y : Q)
   433	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   434	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   435	        Q ⊗[A] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   436	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   437	    ((1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[A] y :
   438	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] Q) ≠ 0 := by
   439	  let p : PrimeSpectrum A :=
   440	    PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)) q
   441	  have hfp : f ∉ p.asIdeal := by
   442	    intro hf
   443	    refine q.isPrime.ne_top (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem q.asIdeal
   444	      (Ideal.mem_comap.mp hf) ?_)
   445	    exact IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit f
   446	  have hp : ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[A] y :
   447	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] Q) ≠ 0 := by
   448	    have h := (TensorProduct.comm A Q p.asIdeal.ResidueField).map_ne_zero_iff.mpr
   449	      (hy p hfp)
   450	    simpa only [TensorProduct.comm_tmul] using h
   451	  have hcom : p.asIdeal =
   452	      q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)) := rfl
   453	  let rho : p.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₐ[A] q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   454	    Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p.asIdeal q.asIdeal
   455	      (Algebra.ofId A (Localization.Away f)) hcom
   456	  have hrho : Function.Bijective rho :=
   457	    (RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_isLocalization (Submonoid.powers f)
   458	      (Localization.Away f)).residueFieldMap_bijective
   459	        p.asIdeal q.asIdeal hcom
   460	  let e : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ≃ₗ[A] q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   461	    LinearEquiv.ofBijective rho.toLinearMap hrho
   462	  have he := (e.rTensor Q).map_ne_zero_iff.mpr hp
   463	  simpa only [LinearEquiv.rTensor_tmul, e, LinearEquiv.ofBijective_apply,
   464	    AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply, map_one] using he

   466	/-- Cancelling an iterated scalar extension preserves a nonzero pure tensor. -/
   467	private theorem one_tmul_one_tmul_ne_zero
   468	    {R S K Q : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Field K]
   469	    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R K] [Algebra S K] [IsScalarTower R S K]
   470	    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q]
   471	    (y : Q) (hy : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[R] y : K ⊗[R] Q) ≠ 0) :
   472	    ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[S] ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] y) :
   473	      K ⊗[S] (S ⊗[R] Q)) ≠ 0 := by
   474	  let e : K ⊗[S] (S ⊗[R] Q) ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R] Q :=
   475	    TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange R S K K Q
   476	  rw [← e.map_ne_zero_iff]
   477	  simpa only [e, TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul,
   478	    one_smul] using hy

   480	/-- Base change of a linear equivalence preserves nonvanishing of a pure tensor. -/
   481	private theorem one_tmul_linearEquiv_ne_zero
   482	    {R K M N : Type u} [CommRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K]
   483	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
   484	    (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (x : M)
   485	    (hx : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[R] x : K ⊗[R] M) ≠ 0) :
   486	    ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[R] e x : K ⊗[R] N) ≠ 0 := by
   487	  let eK := LinearEquiv.baseChange R K M N e
   488	  have h := eK.map_ne_zero_iff.mpr hx
   489	  simpa only [eK, LinearEquiv.baseChange_tmul] using h

   493	/-- A nonzero cohomology class on a field fibre gives a nonzero glued section. -/
   494	private theorem sectionsMapTop_ne_zero_of_one_tmul_ne_zero
   495	    {B K : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Field K]
   496	    [Algebra k K] [Algebra B K] [IsScalarTower k B K]
   497	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
   498	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1)
   499	    (y : Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)
   500	    (hy : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] y : K ⊗[B] Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ≠ 0) :
   501	    D.sectionsMapTop K
   502	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   503	        (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   504	        isTerminalTop D.sheaf y) ≠ 0 := by
   505	  let eDatum := D.datumH0BaseChange K hH1
   506	  have hDatum : eDatum ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] y) ≠ 0 :=
   507	    eDatum.map_ne_zero_iff.mpr hy
   508	  let eSection := Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   509	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C K : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   510	    isTerminalTop (D.baseChange K).sheaf
   511	  have hSection : eSection (eDatum ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] y)) ≠ 0 :=
   512	    eSection.map_ne_zero_iff.mpr hDatum
   513	  rw [← D.linearEquiv₀_datumH0BaseChange_one_tmul K hH1 y]
   514	  exact hSection

   516	/-- A fibrewise-nonzero section remains nonzero after localizing and extending once more
   517	to a residue field of the localized ring. -/
   518	private theorem away_one_tmul_one_tmul_ne_zero
   519	    {R Q : Type u} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q]
   520	    (f : R) (y : Q)
   521	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   522	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   523	        Q ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   524	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   525	    ((1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[Localization.Away f]
   526	      ((1 : Localization.Away f) ⊗ₜ[R] y) :
   527	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[Localization.Away f]
   528	        (Localization.Away f ⊗[R] Q)) ≠ 0 := by
   529	  let B := Localization.Away f
   530	  let K := q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   531	  have hdirect : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[R] y : K ⊗[R] Q) ≠ 0 :=
   532	    fibre_tmul_ne_zero_of_away f y hy q
   533	  exact one_tmul_one_tmul_ne_zero y hdirect
   534	
   535	/-- A generator which is nonzero on every fibre of `D(f)` remains nonzero in every
   536	residue fibre after extending the whole module to `Localization.Away f`.  This is the
   537	orientation consumed by the rank-one local-basis theorem. -/
   538	theorem tensorAwayGenerator_fibre_ne_zero
   539	    {R Q : Type u} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q]
   540	    (f : R) (y : Q)
   541	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   542	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   543	        Q ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   544	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   545	    (((1 : Localization.Away f) ⊗ₜ[R] y) ⊗ₜ[Localization.Away f]
   546	      (1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   547	      (Localization.Away f ⊗[R] Q) ⊗[Localization.Away f]
   548	        q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
   549	  have h := TensorProduct.comm (Localization.Away f)
   550	    q.asIdeal.ResidueField (Localization.Away f ⊗[R] Q) |>.map_ne_zero_iff.mpr
   551	      (away_one_tmul_one_tmul_ne_zero f y hy q)
   552	  simpa only [TensorProduct.comm_tmul] using h

   554	/-- Canonical `H⁰` base change preserves the localized pure tensor's nonvanishing. -/
   555	private theorem h0BaseChange_one_tmul_ne_zero
   556	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   557	    (B K : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   558	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   559	    [Algebra B K] [IsScalarTower k B K]
   560	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   561	    (hy : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y) :
   562	      K ⊗[B] (B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   563	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)) ≠ 0) :
   564	    ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B]
   565	      (P.h0BaseChange B ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y)) :
   566	      K ⊗[B] Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) ≠ 0 := by
   567	  let eH0 : B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ≃ₗ[B]
   568	      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
   569	    P.h0BaseChange B
   570	  exact one_tmul_linearEquiv_ne_zero eH0
   571	    ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y) hy

   573	/-- The canonical scalar-extension certificate package attached to a tied presentation.
   574	
   575	The presentation's own `H¹`-vanishing, finite/projective `H⁰`, and stalk-rank-one fields are
   576	transported along its canonical `h0BaseChange` equivalence.  In particular, the target module
   577	is not replaced by an unrelated witness: it is exactly the datum module of `P.datum.baseChange`.
   578	This is a coefficient-extension feeder for the family producer; it does not assert the missing
   579	native pushforward base-change isomorphism or construct a presentation over a new affine test.
   580	-/
   581	theorem baseChangeRankOneCertificates
   582	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   583	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   584	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   585	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 1) ∧
   586	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) ∧
   587	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) ∧
   588	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
   589	        Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   590	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0
   591	  letI : Module.Finite P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_finite
   592	  letI : Module.Projective P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_projective
   593	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair P.datum).H1 :=
   594	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing
   595	  have hh1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 1) :=
   596	    P.datum.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange B hH1
   597	  let e : B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q ≃ₗ[B]
   598	      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 := P.h0BaseChange B
   599	  letI : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) := by
   600	    infer_instance
   601	  letI : Module.Projective B (B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) := by
   602	    infer_instance
   603	  have hfin : Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) :=
   604	    Module.Finite.equiv e
   605	  have hproj : Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) :=
   606	    Module.Projective.of_equiv e
   607	  have hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
   608	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   609	    intro p
   610	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e, Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange]
   611	    exact P.h0_rank_one (p.comap (algebraMap P.cover.Carrier B))
   612	  exact ⟨hh1, hfin, hproj, hrank⟩
   613	
   614	/-- `H¹`-vanishing in a presentation propagates to every coefficient extension. -/
   615	private theorem datumPair_h1_baseChange
   616	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   617	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   618	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   619	    Subsingleton (datumPair (P.datum.baseChange B)).H1 :=
   620	  (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff (P.datum.baseChange B)).mpr
   621	    (P.baseChangeRankOneCertificates B).1
   622	
   623	/-- The local-away generator supplied over the presentation ring gives the exact
   624	fibrewise-nonvanishing hypothesis required by the divisor construction after localizing.
   625	
   626	This is the missing consumer bridge between the finite-projective generator theorem and
   627	`sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange`.  It compares residue fields across the
   628	localization, cancels the iterated tensor product, and then uses the presentation's
   629	canonical `H⁰` base-change equivalence. -/
   630	theorem sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero
   631	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   632	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   633	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   634	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   635	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   636	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   637	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   638	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   639	    (P.datum.baseChange (Localization.Away f)).sectionsMapTop
   640	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   641	      (P.datumSectionBaseChange (Localization.Away f) y) ≠ 0 := by
   642	  let B := Localization.Away f
   643	  let K := q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   644	  have hiter : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B]
   645	      ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y) :
   646	      K ⊗[B] (B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   647	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)) ≠ 0 :=

    20	`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveH0
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyWindowBaseChange

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

section Tower

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R']
  [IsScalarTower k R R']
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]

private lemma appLE_congr_hom_tower {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f g : X ⟶ Y} (h : f = g)
    {U : Y.Opens} {W : X.Opens} (e : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    f.appLE U W e = g.appLE U W (h ▸ e) := by
  subst h
  rfl

private lemma baseChange_baseChange_tower
    (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
    [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R'']
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi) :
    (D.baseChange R').baseChange R'' = D.baseChange R'' :=
  D.baseChange_baseChange C R R' R''

/-- Comparing a glued section over arbitrary nested opens along `R → R' → R''`
agrees, after transporting the cocycle datum, with direct comparison along `R → R''`. -/
theorem sectionsMap_tower (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi)
    (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
    [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R'']
    {W : (relCurve C R).Opens} {W' : (relCurve C R').Opens}
    {W'' : (relCurve C R'').Opens}
    (hW' : W' ≤ relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ W)
    (hW'' : W'' ≤ relCurveMap C R' R'' ⁻¹ᵁ W')
    (s : ↑(gluedSubmodule R D.pieces D.unit W)) :
    let hD : (D.baseChange R').baseChange R'' = D.baseChange R'' :=
      D.baseChange_baseChange C R R' R''
    let hcomp : W'' ≤ relCurveMap C R R'' ⁻¹ᵁ W := by
      rw [← relCurveMap_comp (C := C) (R := R) (R' := R') (R'' := R''),
        Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
      exact hW''.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono _ hW')
    cast (congrArg (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R'' pi =>
      ↑(gluedSubmodule R'' E.pieces E.unit W'')) hD)
        ((D.baseChange R').sectionsMap R'' hW'' (D.sectionsMap R' hW' s)) =
      D.sectionsMap R'' hcomp s := by
  dsimp only
  simp only [baseChange_baseChange_tower C R R' R'']
  apply Subtype.ext
  funext j
  simp only [sectionsMap_coe]
  have hmaps := Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE
    (relCurveMap C R' R'') (relCurveMap C R R')
    (W ⊓ D.pieces j)
    (W' ⊓ (D.baseChange R').pieces j)
    (W'' ⊓ ((D.baseChange R').baseChange R'').pieces j)
    (D.sectionsMap_component_le R' hW' j)
    ((D.baseChange R').sectionsMap_component_le R'' hW'' j)

/-- The canonical two-step H0 comparison, including reassociation of tensor products and

noncomputable def h0BaseChangeTwoStep

    (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
    [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R''] :
    R'' ⊗[R] Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0 ≃ₗ[R'']
      Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange R'').sheaf 0 :=
  let hD : (D.baseChange R').baseChange R'' = D.baseChange R'' :=
    D.baseChange_baseChange C R R' R''
  ((((TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange R R' R'' R''
      (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)).symm.trans
      (LinearEquiv.baseChange R' R'' _ _ (P.h0BaseChange R'))).trans
      ((P.scalarExtension R').h0BaseChange R'')).trans
      (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv
        (eqToIso (congrArg
          (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R'' pi => E.sheaf) hD)) 0))

    Module.compHom _ (algebraMap R R'')
  letI : IsScalarTower R R'' (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange R'').sheaf 0) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_compHom R R'' _
  apply LinearEquiv.toLinearMap_injective
  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective R

  have hone : P.h0BaseChange R'' ((1 : R'') ⊗ₜ[R] y) =
      h0BaseChangeTwoStep C R R' D P R'' ((1 : R'') ⊗ₜ[R] y) := by

      D.baseChange_baseChange C R R' R''
    let hH1 := (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D).mpr P.h1_vanishing
    let hH1' := (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff (D.baseChange R')).mpr

    change Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv

            (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R'' pi => E.sheaf) hD)) 0

            (LinearEquiv.baseChange R' R'' _ _ (P.h0BaseChange R')

        (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀

    rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]

  subst hf

/-- Comparing glued sections in two stages agrees with direct comparison after transport by the
canonical equality of the two base-changed cocycle data. -/
theorem sectionsMap_tower (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi)
    (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
    [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R'']
    {W : (relCurve C R).Opens} {W' : (relCurve C R').Opens}
    {W'' : (relCurve C R'').Opens}
    (hW' : W' ≤ relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ W)
    (hW'' : W'' ≤ relCurveMap C R' R'' ⁻¹ᵁ W')
    (s : ↑(gluedSubmodule R D.pieces D.unit W)) :
    let hD : (D.baseChange R').baseChange R'' = D.baseChange R'' :=
      D.baseChange_baseChange C R R' R''
    let hcomp : W'' ≤ relCurveMap C R R'' ⁻¹ᵁ W := by
      rw [← relCurveMap_comp (C := C) (R := R) (R' := R') (R'' := R''),
        Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
      exact hW''.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono _ hW')
    cast (congrArg (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R'' pi =>
      ↑(gluedSubmodule R'' E.pieces E.unit W'')) hD)
        ((D.baseChange R').sectionsMap R'' hW'' (D.sectionsMap R' hW' s)) =
      D.sectionsMap R'' hcomp s := by
  let hD : (D.baseChange R').baseChange R'' = D.baseChange R'' :=
    D.baseChange_baseChange C R R' R''
  let hcomp : W'' ≤ relCurveMap C R R'' ⁻¹ᵁ W := by
    rw [← relCurveMap_comp (C := C) (R := R) (R' := R') (R'' := R''),
      Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
    exact hW''.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono _ hW')
  change cast (congrArg (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R'' pi =>
      ↑(gluedSubmodule R'' E.pieces E.unit W'')) hD)
        ((D.baseChange R').sectionsMap R'' hW'' (D.sectionsMap R' hW' s)) =
      D.sectionsMap R'' hcomp s
  apply cast_gluedSubmodule_eq_of_val_heq C hD
  apply Function.hfunext rfl
  intro j j' hj
  cases hj
  let hopen : W'' ⊓ ((D.baseChange R').baseChange R'').pieces j =
      W'' ⊓ (D.baseChange R'').pieces j :=
    congrArg (fun V : (relCurve C R'').Opens => W'' ⊓ V)
      (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces_tower C R R' R'' j)
  apply (Equiv.cast_eq_iff_heq
    (congrArg (fun V : (relCurve C R'').Opens => ↑(Γ(relCurve C R'', V))) hopen)).mp
  simp only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionsMap_coe]
  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE]
  exact cast_appLE_congr
    (relCurveMap_comp (C := C) (R := R) (R' := R') (R'' := R'')) hopen _ _ (s.val j)

/-- Global glued-section comparison is transitive along an arbitrary coefficient tower. -/
theorem sectionsMapTop_tower (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi)
    (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
    [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R'']
    (s : ↑(gluedSubmodule R D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) :
    let hD : (D.baseChange R').baseChange R'' = D.baseChange R'' :=
      D.baseChange_baseChange C R R' R''
    cast (congrArg (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R'' pi =>
      ↑(gluedSubmodule R'' E.pieces E.unit ⊤)) hD)
        ((D.baseChange R').sectionsMapTop R'' (D.sectionsMapTop R' s)) =
      D.sectionsMapTop R'' s := by
  let hW' : (⊤ : (relCurve C R').Opens) ≤
      relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens) := by
    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]
  let hW'' : (⊤ : (relCurve C R'').Opens) ≤
      relCurveMap C R' R'' ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (relCurve C R').Opens) := by
    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]
  simpa only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionsMapTop] using
    sectionsMap_tower C R R' D R'' hW' hW'' s

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

/-!
# Assembly from a rank-one divisor-fibre pullback

This file isolates the last presheaf step in the arbitrary-scheme rank-one fibre construction.
Its input ties an open `W` to the displayed family, supplies native presentations on every
affine pullback, and supplies the canonical evaluation-divisor classifier.  The geometric input
to the assembly theorem is the genuine pullback square of that evaluation divisor along Abel.
The universal property of this stronger square produces, rather than assumes, the factorisation
field of `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`.

The global construction of the canonical classifier and its represented pullbacks remains an
upstream obligation.  The endpoint here keeps that obligation in its geometric `IsPullback`
form and feeds the resulting arbitrary-scheme fibres immediately to
`picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented`.

Thus this module is a conditional assembly interface, not the missing global producer: no
declaration below constructs the evaluator, the open family, or its pullback theorem.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`

  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard

9	/-!
10	# THE SEAM PAIR IS INHABITED, AND ITS INHABITANT IS EXACTLY VANISHING `pic⁰`
11	
12	Four roadmap rows and three file headers in this project defer to one sentence, verbatim:
13	**"inhabitation of the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` is UNMEASURED at every `V` and may be empty
14	everywhere"** (`AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict`, repeated on `…datum.atlas-coupling`, and
15	in `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat`, `Pic0ChartVMonotone`, `Pic0ChartBotRefute`).  Every
16	predecessor result on it is an *endpoint refutation* — the pair fails at `V = ⊤`, is
17	degenerate at `V = ⊥` — and `Pic0ChartSeamCollapse` identifies the pair with `IsIso` of the
18	chart map without exhibiting or refuting one.
19	
20	**This file decides it.**  At the chart whose `rep` slot is filled by the landed degree-zero
21	producer, the pair is *equivalent* to a hypothesis that already has a name elsewhere in the
22	tree:
23	
24	  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f ∧ IsLocallySurjective f  ↔  ∀ S, Subsingleton (pic⁰(S))`
25	
26	Both directions, with no `V`-restriction, no chart index constraint beyond the free `hdeg` at
27	parameter `0`, and no hypothesis on the curve beyond its standing package.
28	
29	## Why this parameter, and why it is not a degenerate dodge
30	
31	The chart is `abelSigmaChartZero` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUseSite.lean`), the Abel
32	chart at parameter `0`, whose `rep` binder is discharged by `divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy`.
33	Its source is the representing object's underlying scheme — and at parameter `0` that object
34	is the *terminal* `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`, so the source is `Spec k` itself and the chart map
35	sends a point `v : T ⟶ Spec k` to the Σ-element `⟨v, class⟩`.
36	
37	That shape is what makes both directions cheap, and in *opposite* ways:
38	
39	* **Antecedent 1 is free**, because the Σ-component of the chart value **is** the point:
40	  reading it off recovers `v`, so the map is injective on the nose at every test
41	  (`injective_abelSigmaChartZero`).  This is not the `V = ⊥` degeneracy — the source is
42	  nonempty and the statement is at the unrestricted chart.
43	* **Antecedent 2 is exactly the vanishing**, because the Σ-component is *surjective* for free
44	  and the fibre component then has to be hit, which at a singleton `pic⁰` it is
45	  (`surjective_app_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton`).  Conversely a *second* degree-zero
46	  class at one test defeats surjectivity, so the vanishing is not merely sufficient
47	  (`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_surjective_app`).
48	
49	So the pair, at this chart, is one hypothesis wearing two hats — and it is the hypothesis
50	`Picard/Pic0VanishingRoute.lean` produces `JacobianData` from by a route with *none* of the
51	atlas's antecedents.  The two routes are not alternatives: they close together.
52	
53	## What is reused rather than rebuilt
54	
55	`Pic0ChartSeamCollapse.chartIso_of_seam` takes `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` and extracts
56	injectivity from it via `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.  Here injectivity is available
57	*directly*, which is strictly less than that antecedent, so the collapse is restated on the
58	weaker input (`chartIso_of_injective`).  That restatement has an independent payoff, recorded
59	below as `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective`: **given coverage, antecedent 1 IS plain
60	elementwise injectivity** — the two-clause `MorphismProperty.relative` reading that
61	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion` prices as a fibre-presentation datum collapses to an
62	injectivity statement once antecedent 2 is in hand.  A lane holding coverage owes injectivity
63	and nothing more.
64	
65	## What this does NOT do
66	
67	* **It does not represent `pic⁰` for a curve of positive genus.**  The hypothesis is false
68	  there — `Picard/Pic0ChartForkNegativeBranch.lean` refutes chart-map injectivity at any field
69	  carrying an effective divisor of the chart degree with two sections, and this file's
70	  `not_seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_two_pic0` is the corresponding refutation of the pair.
71	  That is the *content* of the decision, not a defect of it: the pair is inhabited exactly
72	  where the Jacobian is a point.
73	* **It does not supply the vanishing.**  `genus C = 0 → pic0Subgroup C S = ⊥` is real curve
74	  theory, is the debt `Albanese/Genus0Terminal.lean` isolates, and nothing here proves it.
75	* **It says nothing about a `V` strictly between `⊥` and `⊤` at a positive-genus curve.**  The
76	  interval question those four rows ask is answered *at this parameter only*, and there the
77	  answer is that no restriction is needed: the pair holds at `V = ⊤` under the vanishing.
78	
79	## Main declarations
80	
81	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartIso_of_injective` — the collapse from **plain injectivity** plus
82	  coverage, weakening `chartIso_of_seam`'s first input.
83	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective` — **given coverage, antecedent 1
84	  is elementwise injectivity.**  Chart-free, divisor-free, curve-free.
85	* `AlgebraicGeometry.sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero` — the Σ-component of the terminal
86	  chart's value is the point itself.
87	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_abelSigmaChartZero` — **antecedent 1's elementwise content,
88	  unconditionally**, at the unrestricted chart.
89	* `AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_app_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton` /
90	  `subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_surjective_app` — surjectivity **is** the vanishing, both ways.
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton` — the chart is an isomorphism
92	  of presheaves under the vanishing.
93	* `AlgebraicGeometry.seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton` — **THE INHABITANT**: both
94	  seam antecedents at once.
95	* `AlgebraicGeometry.seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_iff` — **the decision**, as an iff.
96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_two_pic0` — the refutation at any
97	  curve with two distinct degree-zero classes at one test.
98	-/

115	/-! ## The collapse on the weaker input
116	
117	`Pic0ChartSeamCollapse.chartIso_of_seam` derives elementwise injectivity from antecedent 1.
118	Everything after that step uses only the injectivity, so the same proof runs from it — and
119	that matters here because the terminal chart has injectivity *without* having antecedent 1
120	in hand yet. -/

125	/-- **The seam collapse from PLAIN INJECTIVITY.**

132	content of `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective` below, which recovers the stronger form
133	from this one *together with coverage*. -/
134	theorem chartIso_of_injective {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
135	    (hinj : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (f.app T))
136	    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f) :
137	    IsIso (chartSheafHom C f) := by
138	  haveI : Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (chartSheafHom C f).hom :=
139	    Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_of_injective _ _ hinj
140	  haveI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (chartSheafHom C f).hom := hcov
141	  exact (Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso (chartSheafHom C f)).mp
142	    ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

145	/-- **GIVEN COVERAGE, ANTECEDENT 1 IS ELEMENTWISE INJECTIVITY.**
146	
147	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion` prices `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` as a two-clause
148	`MorphismProperty.relative` statement and supplies a fibre-presentation datum
149	(`ChartFibrePresented`) to discharge both clauses.  This says that in the presence of
150	antecedent 2 the whole thing is *one* clause: injectivity on points at every test.
151	
152	The route is the collapse — injective plus locally surjective makes the chart map an
153	isomorphism of sheaves, and `MorphismProperty.relative` contains the isomorphisms.  So the
154	fibre-product representability half of antecedent 1 is not an independent obligation for a
155	lane that already holds coverage.
156	
157	Note the direction of use.  This is *not* a cheaper route to the seam: it consumes antecedent
158	2, which the board prices as the most expensive of the three.  What it does is remove
159	antecedent 1 from the list of things a coverage lane must separately establish, replacing it
160	with a statement about points.  Combined with `injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf`
161	(`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion`, the converse, which needs no coverage) the two are
162	equivalent under coverage. -/
163	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
164	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
165	    (hinj : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (f.app T))
166	    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f) :
167	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
168	  letI : IsIso f := by
169	    haveI := chartIso_of_injective C f hinj hcov
170	    exact (inferInstance : IsIso ((sheafToPresheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (Type u)).map
171	      (chartSheafHom C f)))
172	  exact MorphismProperty.of_isIso (P := IsOpenImmersion.presheaf) f
173	
174	/-! ## The terminal chart at parameter `0`
175	
176	`abelSigmaChartZero` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUseSite.lean`) is the Abel chart whose
177	`rep` binder is discharged by `divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy`, i.e. by the degree-zero
178	producer.  Its representing object is the *terminal* object of the slice, so its source is
179	`Spec k` and the chart's Σ-component is the identity on points.  That single structural fact
180	drives both directions below. -/
181	
182	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi] [IsIntegral (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left]
183	
184	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
185	variable (C pi) in
186	/-- **The Σ-component of the terminal chart's value is the point itself.**
187	
188	`abelSigmaChart` sends `v` to the Σ-element with structure morphism `v ≫ D.hom`
189	(`toSigmaExtension_app_fst`), and at parameter `0` the representing object is
190	`Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`, so `D.hom` is the identity.  Hence reading off the Σ-component
191	recovers `v` on the nose — no transport, no naturality.
192	
193	Everything in this section is this lemma read in one of two directions. -/
194	lemma sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
195	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
196	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
197	    (T : Scheme.{u}) (v : T ⟶ (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).left) :
198	    ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app (op T) v).1 = v := by
199	  change v ≫ 𝟙 _ = v
200	  rw [Category.comp_id]
201	
202	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
203	variable (C pi) in
204	/-- **ANTECEDENT 1'S ELEMENTWISE CONTENT IS UNCONDITIONAL AT THIS CHART**: the terminal chart
205	is injective on points at every test, with no hypothesis whatsoever.
206	
207	Two points a lane must not misread.
208	
209	* This is **not** the `V = ⊥` degeneracy of `isChartUniv_bot`
210	  (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat`).  There the source is the empty scheme and injectivity is
211	  vacuous; here the source is `Spec k`, the chart is **unrestricted** (`V = ⊤` in the
212	  interval literature's coordinates), and the map is injective because the Σ-component
213	  *is* the point.
214	* It is also not in tension with `Pic0ChartForkNegativeBranch`'s refutation of chart-map
215	  injectivity.  That refutation is at a chart of degree `n` with two distinct effective
216	  divisors in one class, which needs `2 ≤ h⁰`; at parameter `0` the functor value is a
217	  singleton (`instSubsingletonDivFamZarSectionZero`), so there is no pair to separate.  The
218	  fork's negative branch and this lemma live at different parameters, and the fork's own
219	  hypothesis `2 ≤ Sheaf.h0` is what keeps them apart. -/
220	theorem injective_abelSigmaChartZero (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
221	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
222	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
223	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
224	    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T) := by
225	  intro v₁ v₂ h
226	  have h₁ := sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg T.unop v₁
227	  have h₂ := sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg T.unop v₂
228	  rw [← h₁, ← h₂, h]
229	
230	/-! ## Surjectivity IS the vanishing
231	
232	The Σ-component being the identity on points means the chart's app is surjective exactly when
233	the fibre components are forced — and there is at most one thing to hit per structure
234	morphism precisely when `pic⁰` is a singleton there.  Both directions below are that
235	observation; neither uses the sheaf property, the site, or a cover. -/
236	
237	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
238	variable (C pi) in
239	/-- **Surjectivity of the terminal chart's app, from vanishing `pic⁰`.**
240	
241	Given a Σ-element `⟨a, ξ⟩` over `T`, the point `a : T ⟶ Spec k` is already a point of the
242	chart source, and its chart value has Σ-component `a` by
243	`sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero`.  The two fibre components then live in the same
244	`pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`, where the hypothesis identifies them — so the transport is
245	`Over.sigmaExtension_ext` with `Subsingleton.allEq`, and no cohomology, cover or naturality
246	enters. -/
247	theorem surjective_app_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton
248	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
249	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
250	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
251	    (hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S))
252	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
253	    Function.Surjective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T) := by
254	  rintro ⟨a, xi⟩
255	  refine ⟨a, ?_⟩
256	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C)
257	    (show a ≫ 𝟙 _ = a from Category.comp_id a) ?_
258	  exact (hvan _).allEq _ _
259	
260	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
261	variable (C pi) in
262	/-- **THE CONVERSE: surjectivity FORCES the vanishing.**
263	
264	If the chart's app is surjective at the test `S.left`, then every degree-zero class over
265	`Over.mk S.hom` — i.e. over `S` itself, since `Over.mk S.hom = S` by `rfl` — is the chart
266	value of some point, and by the previous lemma's Σ-component computation that point is
267	`S.hom` itself.  So the class is determined, and two classes over `S` coincide.
268	
269	This is what makes the decision an equivalence rather than a sufficient condition, and it is
270	the reason this file's headline is not a weakening: a curve with two distinct degree-zero
271	classes at one test has no hope at this chart, whatever `V` one restricts to
272	(`not_seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_two_pic0`). -/
273	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_surjective_app
274	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
275	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
276	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
277	    (hsurj : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ,
278	      Function.Surjective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T))
279	    (S : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
280	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S) := by
281	  refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
282	  -- both classes name a Σ-element over `S.left` with structure morphism `S.hom`
283	  obtain ⟨vx, hvx⟩ := hsurj (op S.left) ⟨S.hom, x⟩
284	  obtain ⟨vy, hvy⟩ := hsurj (op S.left) ⟨S.hom, y⟩
285	  -- the Σ-components pin the two points to `S.hom`, hence to each other
286	  have hx : vx = S.hom := by
287	    rw [← sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg S.left vx, hvx]
288	  have hy : vy = S.hom := by
289	    rw [← sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg S.left vy, hvy]
290	  have : (⟨S.hom, x⟩ : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S.left)) = ⟨S.hom, y⟩ := by
291	    rw [← hvx, ← hvy, hx, hy]
292	  exact eq_of_heq (Sigma.mk.inj this).2

294	/-! ## THE INHABITANT, AND THE DECISION
295	
296	The two sections above meet here.  Injectivity is free, surjectivity is the vanishing, and
297	`isIso_iff_bijective` at every test turns the pair into `IsIso` — from which both seam
298	antecedents follow, antecedent 1 because `MorphismProperty.relative` contains the isomorphisms
299	and antecedent 2 because an iso is locally surjective. -/
300	
301	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
302	variable (C pi) in
303	/-- **The terminal chart is an isomorphism of presheaves under the vanishing.**
304	
305	The bridge lemma of this section: injective (free) plus surjective (the vanishing) at every
306	test is bijective at every test, and a pointwise-iso natural transformation is an iso. -/
307	theorem isIso_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton
308	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
309	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
310	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
311	    (hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S)) :
312	    IsIso (abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg) := by

arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine

* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the

/-! ## The degree at a field point -/

/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))

section DegAt

variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
@[simp]
theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]

/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]

/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
  rfl

/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
